headline: Form and function,
the same answer.
hero.intro: I'm Mona Abishek. I taught myself to build software, and I care most about the details you're not supposed to notice.

story.label: 01 — The long way round
story.heading: I have a habit of arriving at things late, and on my own.
paragraphs: In the fourth grade I wanted a guitar I couldn't afford. I bought one in college and taught myself to play from YouTube, one clumsy chord at a time. I still can't read sheet music. I can play almost anything I love.

In the eighth grade a coach left me off the football team. I didn't play again for years. I started again last year — twice a month, badly, completely happy. I watch the game now the way I watch everything: for the tactics underneath, the part most people don't look at.

I started university in electrical engineering. By the second year I knew it wasn't mine, so I taught myself to code — Udemy, YouTube, strangers on the internet — and walked into the job anyway. Nobody handed me this. I prefer it that way.
I'm drawn to the 911 that doesn't look like much and quietly outruns everything around it. That's the kind of work I'm trying to make.

principles.label: 02 — How I work
principles.heading: A few things I don't compromise on.

items.title: Form and function are one decision.
items.body: If how it works and how it feels disagree, I'm not finished yet.

items.title: No shortcuts I'd be ashamed of.
items.body: Nolan builds the spinning hallway for real. I'd rather do the honest, harder version too.

items.title: The details are the whole thing.
items.body: Good work rewards a closer look. Most people won't take it. The right ones will.

items.title: Learn it by doing it.
items.body: I don't wait for a syllabus or permission. I find the edge of what I know and push past it.

work.label: 03 — Work
work.heading: Where I do this for a living.

roles.summary: Full-stack work on internal scientific platforms — the systems researchers use to make sense of compound data, serving 2,000+ users and handling ~9K queries/day.
highlights: Designed and integrated GraphQL schemas for 8 heterogeneous data sources (REST APIs, Elasticsearch), building complete backend data layers with concurrency-controlled API fetching, Redis caching, and graceful fallbacks for deprecated upstream services.

Built 3 data-rich feature modules from scratch with search views, detail pages, interactive data grids, cross-linked navigation, and intelligent search suggestions; cut page load time by 25% by splitting monolithic GraphQL queries and deferring heavy fragments.

Led the end-to-end migration of CI/CD pipelines (frontend + backend) from Jenkins to GitHub Actions; configured Kubernetes HPA to auto-scale pods on CPU/memory thresholds; added SonarQube and Sentry for quality gating and runtime monitoring.

Built a bi-directional vendor integration (Python, Celery, AWS SQS) handling 4 entity types — outbound event payloads and inbound REST callback handlers with status-lifecycle mapping, interaction logging, and retry logic, enabling capabilities the legacy desktop application could not support.

Built a full-stack POC in ~50 hours to replace a paid vendor SaaS product using AI-powered agentic workflows (React, Node.js, PostgreSQL); pitched to senior leadership and secured executive approval for production build, now in active development.

items.name: Orchestrator
items.tagline: A control layer for the age of AI agents.
items.description: An open-source orchestration tool for AI coding agents — zero SDK or instrumentation required. Streams a real-time Kanban dashboard showing every execution step, tool call, and token count. Includes token-budget enforcement that auto-pauses agents mid-execution on limit breach, and a background watchdog for stuck sessions. Published on npm: a single npx command boots the full stack.

items.name: Melthify
items.description: An AI-powered mental-health platform with an OpenAI API chatbot for private, real-time conversational support and an anonymous community layer, deployed on Firebase. An early one — built to help, and to learn.

items.name: xshare-SSN
items.tagline: A campus-only place to share moments.
items.description: A social platform exclusive to SSN students. A scalable Node/Express/MongoDB backend, AWS S3 for media, Redux-managed React on the front, JWT and bcrypt holding the door. Built before placements to prove I could ship something real.

offTheClock.label: 05 — Off the clock
offTheClock.heading: What I notice when no one's paying me to.

items.body: I love cars the way some people love buildings — for the engineering you can feel. Formula 1 most of all: the precision, the impossible detail, drivers working at the edge of what's survivable.
An acoustic, self-taught, other people's songs. No audience. Just me, working out something I love until my fingers remember it without being asked.
Interstellar's docking scene. The moment the twin walks out in The Prestige. I love stories that fold back on themselves and reward a second watch. I'm trying to build the same way.
Cut from the team at thirteen; back on the pitch a decade later. Twice a month, for the love of a tough, risky, beautiful game and the tactics humming underneath it.

items.v: Orchestrator — a control layer for AI-agent workflows.
Going deeper on agentic systems and the tooling around them.
A fingerstyle arrangement I'm not quite good enough for yet.
F1 race weekends, and far too much football.
A team that sweats the details as much as I do.

contact.label: 07 — Contact
contact.heading: If any of this stayed with you.
contact.blurb: I'm looking for a team that builds things worth looking closely at. If that sounds like yours, I'd like to talk.

lines: This site wasn't typed so much as directed — built the way I build now: orchestrating, reviewing, and refusing to settle until the details were right. Every word here is mine.

easterEgg.pledgeText: Everything here looks ordinary. A name, some work, a few things I love.
easterEgg.turnText: But you looked closer than most people do. That was the whole point.

keywords.text: the one that doesn't look like much.
